name: buddy
description: Claude Code buddy plugin: Quack the ASCII duck waddles above your prompt and talks back — or bring back your /buddy

character.title: Which character to show (see the personality tab in /buddy)
character.description: The id of the character drawn above your prompt, such as duck or cat. A pick in the personality tab of /buddy overrides it on this machine; picking this same character there returns to it.

customCharactersDir.title: customCharactersDir: the folder of your own characters (optional)
customCharactersDir.description: A folder of character files, one {id}.json each, following the plugin's schema/character.schema.json. They join the built-in characters in the personality tab of /buddy; one with the same id as a built-in replaces it. Leave empty to use only the built-in characters.

walkOverPromptBar.title: Walk back and forth over the prompt bar
walkOverPromptBar.description: On: the character walks over the prompt bar, on the line above your prompt. Off: it stays in one place and only animates there.

commentAfterEachTurn.title: commentAfterEachTurn: the buddy comments after each of Claude's answers (uses tokens)
commentAfterEachTurn.description: After every answered turn, one short call on model reads the last chatTurnsToRead turns of your chat and writes commentAfterEachTurn, one line in the character's voice for its speech bubble. The same call also writes suggestNextPrompt when that is on. secondsBetweenComments spaces commentAfterEachTurn out. Off: the buddy stays quiet after turns.

model.title: Model the buddy uses (opus, sonnet, haiku, a model id, or inherit)
model.description: The model behind every buddy call: commentAfterEachTurn, suggestNextPrompt and the answer to every /buddy question. Give an alias (opus, sonnet, haiku) or a full model id. inherit uses whatever model your chat is on, read at each call, and opus when it cannot be read.

effort.title: How hard the buddy's model thinks: low, medium, high, xhigh, max or inherit
effort.description: The thinking effort of every buddy call, on the model option's model. Higher is slower and costs more. inherit uses the effort of your chat's latest request; before its first request, or when that request sets none or a number, no effort is sent and the model's own default applies.

secondsBetweenComments.title: Fewest seconds between two commentAfterEachTurn (0 = after every answer)
secondsBetweenComments.description: With commentAfterEachTurn on, a new commentAfterEachTurn waits at least this many seconds after the previous one. 0 says one after every answered turn. It does not space out suggestNextPrompt, which is written every turn.

suggestNextPrompt.title: The buddy suggests your next prompt (uses tokens)
suggestNextPrompt.description: After every answered turn, the same short call on model proposes your next prompt, as you would type it, as the grey suggestion in the prompt box. Claude Code's own suggestion is held back and shown only when the buddy has none. Off: Claude Code's own suggestion shows as usual.

chatTurnsToRead.title: How many recent chat turns the buddy remembers (1 to 10)
chatTurnsToRead.description: The buddy's memory: your chat's latest answered turns (your prompt and Claude's answer), each with what the buddy showed after it (its commentAfterEachTurn and suggestNextPrompt) and your /buddy questions with its answers. Every buddy call reads it; the buddy knows it remembers only this far and says so when asked about anything older. Kept per session and per character. More turns, more tokens per call.

logLevel.title: How much the plugin logs: error, info or debug
logLevel.description: What the plugin writes to logFile. error: failures only. info: also sessions, commands, questions and their outcomes, commentAfterEachTurn and menu picks. debug: also question text, the shape of model results and drawing decisions. It never logs who you are.

logFile.title: Where the plugin log goes (empty = no log file)
logFile.description: The default follows CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR: $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/buddy/buddy.log when it is set, ~/.claude/buddy/buddy.log when it is not. A path you give is used as written, with ~ as your home folder and a leading $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR as the config folder. One JSON line per record, capped at 1 MB with one older copy (.1); /buddy log shows its path and last 20 lines. Empty: no log file; failures still go to Claude Code's debug log.

saveRounds.title: Keep a file per turn of what went into buddy and came out
saveRounds.description: For seeing what the buddy sees and says: one text file per main-chat turn, in the chat's own folder beside its transcript ({config}/projects/{project}/{session id}/buddy/, next to memory.json, the buddy's memory of that chat). At most 150 per chat (round-001.txt to round-150.txt, the least recently written overwritten once all are used; ls -t lists them newest first), each holding, in the order it happened, from the turn's start to the next turn's start: the prompt the turn began with, each tool call buddy heard with its arguments and output (each value cut at 500 characters), every buddy log record at any level, each bubble line and prompt-box suggestion, the turn's end as buddy filed it into its memory, and every model call buddy made, its system prompt, prompt and reply verbatim. They hold what the transcript beside them holds: your prompts, Claude's answers and tool output. Off: no round files.

ambiguousCharacterWidth.title: Width of ambiguous-width characters in your terminal: narrow or wide
ambiguousCharacterWidth.description: Some characters (East Asian ambiguous width) take one column in most terminals and two in some, often with a CJK locale. narrow: 1 column; wide: 2. The speech bubble and the character are laid out to match. Change it only if the bubble's border looks misaligned.
